inducedVerdict.assessment: The CONSTRUCT_INDUCED verdicts survive adversarial scrutiny for 12 of the 13 cited instances; one should be reclassified. I re-read five cited transcripts verbatim (20260604-224457/adopt-existing-standard-pair, 20260602-185022/recipe-laravel-showcase-fullstack, 20260513-133625/launch-production-from-standard-pair, 20260518-135551/api-node-postgres-classic-dev) plus the handler code (internal/workflow/adopt.go, engine.go:465-470, validate.go, recipe_shape.go). The decisive evidence is that ZCP itself subsequently classified most of these bounces as its own defects by shipping fixes: CanonicalBareForm equivalence matching for the 2026-05-18 composite-schema rejections (platform import accepted bare forms the whole time — the check enforced ZCP's stored schema copy, stricter than the authority, violating ZCP's own 'live platform is the source of truth' contract); the R3-P1 RecipeShape worker slot for the 'no recipe service matches' bounces; dev-only narrowing (RecipeNarrowDevOnly, task #52) for the kanban refusal; and the bootstrapMode-required fix whose code comment (validate.go:27-31) explicitly names the old empty-to-standard default as a trap. The worst cascade (20260602 t6, 11 turns) is verified line-by-line: ZCP's own recipe import YAML was the tell, its live-type matcher the check, they drifted; the construct then ACCEPTED a planless discover-complete (transcript line 106) and bounced provision on the missing plan two turns later with a wrong recovery pointer ('Start bootstrap first' while the session was active) — the construct manufactured the state it rejected, so the provision plan-gate's local legitimacy does not rescue the round-trips. The launch verb-routing bounces are pure taxonomy tax: identical semantic payloads succeeded via action=start immediately after bouncing via action=complete, with an error misattributing the workflow ('bootstrap complete: bootstrap not active'). STEELMAN RESULTS: (1) The adopt pairing gate has a genuine protective rationale — adopt.go documents that silently committing two dev containers dead-ended launch's git-push gate (Wave-1 finding), and refusing to parse pairing from free-text intent prose is correct policy (prose is not a typed commitment channel). The INDUCED verdict nonetheless holds on delivery grounds: ZCP's blessed scope= input structurally cannot carry the decision, the route-menu had already enumerated the exactly-2 same-type adoptables before the doomed call (so the choice + templates could be surfaced upfront in the session-active response, removing the bounce while keeping the explicit election), the error's own suggestion field circularly recommends the scope= form that just bounced, and the gate condition len(adoptable)==2 means the riskier 3-adoptable case commits silently (verified live at 20260602 line 171: appdev/appstage/workerstage, all alpine/php-nginx@8.4, committed as 3 independent dev containers unprompted) — so the bounce is shape-correlated, not risk-correlated. Any fix must retain the explicit pairing election; the induced element is the post-hoc error channel, not the refusal to guess. (2) The resumable-stale-state instances are fixture-seeded, but the verdict holds because the construct demonstrably produces the identical planless-complete state in live operation (20260602 line 106) and the advertise-resumable-then-bounce-with-wrong-pointer behavior is its own regardless of state provenance; this is the weakest sub-bucket. (3) classic-static-nginx-simple t4 FAILS the strict three-prong test and should be reclassified: bootstrapMode is genuinely required information, and ZCP's own fix kept the bounce and corrected the diagnostic rather than removing the round-trip — a once-bouncing omitted-required-field with a now-correct pointer is protective elicitation with a diagnostic-quality defect, not a manufactured round-trip. The classifier itself flagged it borderline.

If other uncited instances in the 63 share this exact shape (omitted required field, single bounce, fix-was-message-only), they should move with it; none of the other 12 cited instances do. All other cited verdicts stand, with two annotations rather than reclassifications: (a) adopt-pairing instances stay INDUCED but the corrective must preserve the explicit pairing election (surface the choice + templates proactively at session-active when the adoptable set is exactly 2 same-type, and fix the circular scope= suggestion) — never auto-commit from intent prose; (b) discover-adoption-state-resumable instances stay INDUCED on the strength of in-corpus proof that the construct creates the same planless state live, but should carry a fixture-seeded-provenance flag.

inducedVerdict.assessment:
The CONSTRUCT_INDUCED verdict set does NOT survive intact: 4 of the 9 cited exemplars reclassify under adversarial scrutiny, including the three instances (1, 3, 7) that anchor the headline 6-8-turn detours — so the 19/26 (73%) induced rate is materially inflated. However, a genuine construct-induced core (5/9) survives decisively and should be kept.

WHAT SURVIVES (genuine induced):
(a) Instance 5 — smoking gun, transcript-verified (eval/behavioral/runs/20260605-032130/git-push-setup-with-cicd-method-prompt, lines 226→248): build-integration's needsGitPushSetup nextStep literally instructs `git-push-setup service="appstage"` (internal/tools/workflow_build_integration.go:182 echoes input.Service), which git-push-setup then refuses with the stage-half error. ZCP authored the exact call it refused.
(b) Instances 2/4 (stage-half redirects) — code-verified purposeless: workflow_git_push_setup.go:380 sets pushHost := meta.Hostname, so every side effect (probe, origin-sync, env write, restart, meta stamp via pair-keyed UpdateServiceMeta) is identical whichever pair hostname is passed. The sibling build-integration accepts the stage hostname and corrects via pushSource/topologyNote (addTopologyFields, whose own doc-comment acknowledges agents pass stage hostnames). The handler doc-comment imports deploy-side rationale ("same source-of-push remediation as the deploy handlers"), but deploy-side risk (pushing artifacts FROM a stage container) does not exist at the setup surface — no push happens. Accept-and-report (the sibling's pattern, and CLAUDE.md's own "reconcile to truth + report" contract) removes the bounce with zero safety loss.
(c) Instance 8 — transcript-verified (20260603-201645): the empty-plan adopt auto-derive silently committed ubuntu/nodejs@22 + alpine/nodejs@22 as two independent ModeDev metas against the agent's explicit "standard dev/stage pair" attestation, violating ZCP's own pinned pairing-never-guessed invariant (composite-bare equivalence gap post Sunday-release migration); git-push-setup then rejected ZCP's own committed state, and the remedy bounced AGAIN (plan-in-action=start refusal, line 77). Corroborated by ZCP's own remediation: the composite-aware guard ("share runtime base nodejs@22 — ZCP will not guess") landed in commit 1d36eb73 as an eval-loop root-cause fix, and fires correctly in the 20260605 run.
(d) Instance 9 — holds moderately: the remedy was a pure ZCP-metadata relabel (dev→simple via 3-call re-adopt) — same container, same code, same repo; flipping a ZCP enum made the push acceptable. The ModeDev×push-git ban is asserted, not argued, in the archived deploy-strategy plan (§3.2 comment: "ModeDev is invalid combo with push-git"), and the launch chain itself demanded the action its own gate refused.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE:
(e) Instances 1, 3, 7 (ADOPT_REQUIRED "not bootstrapped" → adopt ceremony) — the classifier's core premise ("the adopt route auto-derives the same plan from live discovery, proving the data was already obtainable without ceremony") is factually wrong for these exact fixtures. All three have two same-base nodejs runtimes — exactly the case where auto-derive REFUSES to guess pairing (ErrAdoptPairingChoice, internal/workflow/adopt.go:88-102, observed firing live in 20260605-032130 line 160, pinned by the adopt-plan tests). Instance 8 is the classifier's own proof of why silent derivation is unsafe: when the derive did guess, it manufactured a worse bounce. A redesign cannot remove the round-trip without losing safety — the pairing decision is real, consequential (it determines the push source that receives SSH origin-sync + GIT_TOKEN + restart), and non-derivable. Bootstrap additionally does load-bearing platform work the cited tasks needed: in 20260515-154213, /var/www/appdev (working tree + git, via InitServiceGit) appears only post-adopt — the agent had spent ~15 turns failing to locate code and needed the tree to write the workflow file, commit, and push. The legitimate residue is recovery COST (route-menu + provision-attest theater for adopt-of-existing ≈ 3 ceremony calls around 1 real decision, plus the older SERVICE_NOT_FOUND/recovery=status shape giving no route) — a UX-cost/recovery-quality finding, not "bounce served no protective/platform purpose."
(f) Instance 6 (and its sibling turn-4/turn-6 payloads) — reclassifies to knowledgeGap. The call as made was genuinely invalid for the goal: build-integration configures SOURCE-project CI, and no amount of adopting source services would configure the launched production project's pipeline. The defect is a missing surface (nothing in ZCP addresses the prod project's pipeline post-launch) plus a goal-blind ADOPT_REQUIRED recovery steering at a useless adopt — a tell/guidance gap, not a removable round-trip; even the ideal response ends at the dashboard walkthrough the agent eventually delivered.

NET: the construct genuinely manufactures bounces where its OWN surfaces disagree (sibling addressability inconsistency, nextStep-authored refusals, derive-vs-gate divergence, label-only mode gates). It does NOT manufacture the adopt-registration bounces over ambiguous pairs — those carry a real decision the construct correctly refuses to guess. The corrected induced rate among the 26 discretionary instances is roughly 10-12 (≈40-45%), not 19 (73%).

inducedVerdict.assessment: The CONSTRUCT_INDUCED verdicts survive adversarial scrutiny. I re-read three cited transcripts end-to-end (20260505-151844 greenfield turns 61-64, 20260603-232540 nextjs turns 35-43, 20260521-084854 cadence turns 83-100) plus the kept import gate (internal/tools/import.go::gateOverrideOnFailedHistory), the verdict doc (plans/deploy-gate-category-error-2026-06-04.md), and the fix commits (17efbf9a deploy-gate deletion, 09d4dd0f R6 corrective). Steelman attempted: the DIAGNOSIS_REQUIRED bounce is fired by the import-override gate — the one gate ZCP deliberately kept, sanctioned by the published docs contract, and in the cadence instance it surfaced real collateral (wouldDestroy.envVars listed user-set NEXTAUTH_URL). The steelman fails at the instance level on all three test-criteria: (1) Agent intent was reasonable — every instance is a corrective redeploy with a verified pre-existing fix (e.g. 20260603: Write public/favicon.ico at turn 36 BEFORE the first refusal at turn 37); a failed deploy is non-destructive per ZCP's own classifier, so redeploy was the correct move. (2) The bounce served no protective purpose in any instance — in the early suites the deploy refusal's recovery hint LITERALLY prescribed the destructive call (verbatim in two transcripts: recovery={tool: zerops_import, args: {override: "true", startWithoutCode: "true"}}), so the import gate was bouncing ZCP's own prescription; in the later suites the agent fully complied with the prescribed zerops_events (which returned the same failureClassification the failed-deploy response already carried), was refused byte-identically (the gate had no ack/satisfied-state parameter — structural deadlock), and reached override as the only exit; every ack was a rubber stamp of a diagnosis already in hand. Even the NEXTAUTH_URL surfacing averted nothing — the chain left no non-destructive path and the var was wiped anyway. (3) The redesign removed the bounce without losing safety — shipped (17efbf9a): corrective redeploys now proceed ungated, the import-override gate remains for genuinely chosen overrides, and Wave 7 re-tested the exemplar scenario green; in the NEXTAUTH_URL counterfactual the redesign strictly increases safety (no override occurs, env var preserved). The "agents omitted startWithoutCode = knowledge gap" reclassification angle also fails: ZCP's own early recovery args carried startWithoutCode=true, and R6 later added retryCall+startWithoutCode patchHints to the import gate precisely because the corrective was incomplete — ZCP owned that information and under-delivered it. Archaeology confirms no missed protective rationale: the deploy gate was a vestige of the Wave-1 auto-override recovery, its own doc-comment argued against gating corrective redeploys, it contradicted ZCP's published contract (only delete + import-override are confirmation-gated; "a bad deploy is fixed by another deploy"), and the transcript survey found zero positive instances.

inducedVerdict.assessment:
I re-read three cited transcripts (20260515-145539/launch-production-dev-only, 20260604-071303/export-buildfromgit-self-snapshot, 20260513-133625/launch-production-from-standard-pair) and the handler/router code. I attempted four steelmen; all fail, and two collapse on code-level evidence the classifier didn't even cite.

LAUNCH VERB INSTANCES (7 of 10). Steelman 1 — "the stateless accumulator (re-call action=start with full inputs) is a deliberate design with compaction-recovery/idempotency rationale, so the classify/complete bounces are the agent ignoring the protocol." Refuted on timing and on substance. (a) Timing: the guidance the agents saw at classify-prompt (fallback atom export-classify-envs, as of 0bbec747) says only "re-calling with `envClassifications` populated" / "call back with an envClassifications map" — it never names the verb. The action enum on zerops_workflow lists `classify` as a valid action (internal/tools/workflow.go:46). An agent at status="classify-prompt" choosing action=classify is the maximally natural reading. The atom that explicitly warns 'There is NO `action="classify"` step (that's the recipe-fact workflow — wrong tool). There is NO `action="complete"` step (that's bootstrap)' was created 2026-05-20 (commit 3e45cd8f) — AFTER every cited launch run (05-13, 05-15, 05-18). The construct's own maintainers acknowledged the collision and patched the TELL while leaving the trap in the router: today workflow.go:499-504 still routes action=classify unconditionally to handleRecipeClassify, ignoring the workflow=launch-production param the call carries; workflow_classify.go:44-50 then demands factType with recipe-writer vocabulary ("gotcha_candidate, ig_item_candidate, ...") — actively misleading for a launch agent. (b) Substance: in 145539 the identical envClassifications payload bounced at t4/t5 was accepted VERBATIM at t8 via action=start — the bounce protected literally nothing. The complete bounce ("Step is required... step=\"discover\"", workflow.go:409-421 falling through to handleBootstrapComplete) is bootstrap vocabulary emitted mid-launch. A workflow-aware rejection or verb aliasing keeps the accumulator design intact and removes the churn — redesign loses zero safety. This is also a direct violation of the project's own information contract (CLAUDE.md: one owner per concept; the R6 retryCall convention shows the house standard for refusals — none of these bounces carried a correct nextCall).

WORST CASCADE (20260513-133625, t3). The weakest instance on agent-reasonableness (classify with no workflow param at scope-prompt), but the 11-turn cost is dominated by THREE construct surfaces compounding: the misleading factType suggestion, the bootstrap-vocabulary complete bounce, and — decisive — action=status returning "Phase: idle ... not bootstrapped ... Bootstrap is two-phase" while a launch was mid-flight, because the launch state file is only persisted at the classify-prompt→ready-to-launch transition (launch_p_lp_3_test.go) so the canonical recovery primitive (CLAUDE.md P4: "Lifecycle recovery is via action=status") is BLIND to early-phase launches and affirmatively steered the agent into the unnecessary bootstrap-adopt detour. Transcript confirms launch had already accepted scope at call #1 pre-detour; post-detour the same start call (#12) advanced normally. INDUCED holds.

EXPORT INSTANCES (3 of 10). Steelman 2 — "the no-bootstrapped-meta refusal protects bundle correctness: topology.Mode is unguessable from the platform, pairing is genuinely ambiguous (ubuntu/ vs alpine/nodejs@22), and ServiceMeta is the single owner." This is the strongest steelman and the classifier pre-conceded the pairing point — but it collapses at code level. The refusal text (workflow_export.go:130: "export needs the topology.Mode ... to resolve variant") is contradicted by the code: (a) the ONE place mode lands in the bundle, ops/bundle/helpers.go:164-166 runtimeImportMode(_ topology.Mode), IGNORES its argument and emits constant NON_HA; (b) the only real consumer is setupCandidatesFor (workflow_export_probe.go:149) which merely biases setup-NAME matching order, with safe fallbacks — single-setup yaml is taken regardless of mode, multi-setup ambiguity yields an actionable error listing available setups, and a direct-ask path already exists (Setup input / set-default-setup / requiresSetupInput blocker); (c) meta.RemoteURL is an explicitly non-fatal cache — the bundle's repoURL comes from a live SSH read. Worst case without meta is an actionable setup-name prompt, never a silently wrong bundle. So the gate's protective claim fails, and the remedy it forces — a full 3-call bootstrap-adopt session with route-menu, session commit, pairing bounce, plan, and a provision attestation over already-ACTIVE services ("no new provisioning needed", transcript #7) — is ~4 turns of pure ceremony around at most 1 turn of genuine decision content (the pairing question, which export's own scope-prompt/classify-prompt narrowing mechanism could host). Reproduced identically across three runs on three days. Steelman 3 — "downstream git-push-setup chain needs meta anyway" — true but that gate fires at its own seam with its own remedy; export pre-paying it is not protection for THIS bounce. Steelman 4 — "a pinning test (workflow_export_test.go:620) proves it's deliberate" — deliberate ≠ protective; no spec invariant in docs/spec-workflows.md §9/§10 justifies the hard gate (P-LP-10's meta dependency is launch's buildFromGit provenance, not export's — export reads the live remote).

One honest caveat that does NOT flip verdicts: turns_to_recover in the 05-15/05-18 launch instances is somewhat inflated by stale sibling launch state (myapp-prod/api-prod/eval-zcp-prod) left in the shared eval project by earlier runs — but findActiveLaunchState surfacing a stale sibling as the agent's own "ready-to-launch" without matching productionProjectName is itself construct recovery behavior, not agent error.

All ten CONSTRUCT_INDUCED verdicts survive: reasonable intent (verbatim-accepted payloads, semantically-invited verbs), no protective purpose (collision handler for a different sub-system; gate justification contradicted by its own emit code), and safety-preserving redesigns exist (workflow-aware classify routing or verb alias; export treating missing meta as no-bias with its existing setup-resolution fallbacks, or a 1-turn mode/pairing prompt in export's own narrowing).

inducedVerdict.assessment:
The 9-instance INDUCED set does not survive intact: 4 of 9 reclassify, including one resting on a factually wrong premise. The core construct critique DOES survive in narrowed form (5 instances), anchored by evidence no steelman explains away.

REFUTED instances (round-trip NOT manufactured by the construct):
(1) greenfield-node-postgres 20260503-114249 and (2) 20260503-125036 — I diffed the transcripts: both bounced plans carried empty bootstrapMode and no stageHostname. Empty mode defaults to standard (spec-workflows.md §2.3), and internal/workflow/validate.go:377-388 hard-fails standard mode without explicit stageHostname. Under the classifier's own proposed redesign (accept plan at start, validate content), these plans bounce anyway — with a targeted error instead of a shape error, same turn count. The round-trip was inevitable; its cause was missing ZCP plan vocabulary, not parameter placement. → knowledgeGap.
(3) develop-add-managed-dep 20260604-001223 — valkey@8 is NOT in the catalog (the embedded import schema enumerates only valkey@7.2); catalogTypeErrors (validate.go:372) rejects it under any design. Round-trip inevitable → knowledgeGap.
(4) classic-go-simple 20260604-200145 — the classifier's premise "invalid type (golang@1)" is factually WRONG: golang@1 IS in the catalog enum (alongside go@1, go@1.22, golang@1.22). The bounced plan {app, golang@1, bootstrapMode=dev} was content-VALID — accept-and-validate would have provisioned a dev-mode mutable container against the scenario's simple-mode intent, a semantic miss no validator catches. The bounce + discover-step mode taxonomy demonstrably corrected it (verified transcript diff: turn 18 dev/golang@1 → turn 30 simple/go@1.22). This instance fails the rubric's "bounce served no protective/platform purpose" test outright. → knowledgeGap.

HELD instances (construct genuinely manufactures the round-trip):
(5) 20260605-024523 — verified byte-identical resubmission (JSON-normalized compare of the bounced start plan vs the complete step=discover plan: True). (6) 20260605-033339 — verified byte-identical. (7) 20260604-205605 — bounced plan was complete and catalog-valid (postgresql@16 IS in the enum); resubmission changed only pg16→pg18, a discretionary refresh. (8) 20260604-210341 — bounced plan valid; resubmission merely dropped redundant-but-legal dep mode fields. For these four, the strongest steelman is the gate's genealogy: commit c20f9e77 shows the rejection replaced a SILENT DROP (schema accepted plan at start and discarded it; the fizzy-log agent hit "provision requires plan" three calls later). That history justifies not-silently-ignoring — it does not justify rejection over acceptance. The full validator (ValidateBootstrapTargets: catalog types, stageHostname, hostname collisions, locks) runs at the discover commit and could run identically on an inline plan at start; spec invariants B5/B8 (plan must come through the discover commit point) are satisfied by an atomic start+complete-discover; the catalog attach (populateStacks at workflow.go:1007) could ride a targeted validation bounce. No safety property depends on the shape rejection itself.
(9) mount 20260504-104436 — holds. guard.go:38-42 states the gate's purpose explicitly: "ensure the agent has received knowledge before performing infrastructure operations" — a knowledge-delivery gate, not a safety gate. The project's own gate convention (CLAUDE.md) reserves hard gates for "genuinely-destructive or impossible operations"; mounting a live service is neither. The transcript proves zero protective effect: after the 3-turn bounce chain (mount WORKFLOW_REQUIRED → develop-start PREREQUISITE_MISSING → status), the agent read the identical filesystem over plain ssh appdev ungated. Reasonable read intent, no protection, redesign (allow mount on live services, or downgrade to advisory) loses nothing SSH doesn't already give away.

Net: the classifier's structural diagnosis of the plan-at-start shape rejection is correct — it is content-blind and taxes fully valid plans on the most common greenfield path — but it over-attributed: in 4 of 8 plan bounces the plan was content-defective (or semantically wrong in a way only the discover materials could fix) and the round-trip would have existed under the proposed redesign too. The classifier's "corrections came from discover-step materials ZCP could attach to the route-menu" argument is a delivery improvement worth pursuing, but it is counterfactual speculation, not evidence the bounce served no purpose as-built.
